issues.title: Tailwind classes in incorrect order
issues.description: Tailwind utility classes must follow standard ordering: layout, positioning, sizing, spacing (margin before padding), typography, visual effects. The classes have padding (pr-2) before margin (mt-[-16px]), which violates this convention.
issues.rule_name: Tailwind CSS Classes Must Follow Standard Ordering

issues.title: Missing optional chaining causes runtime error when openForm is undefined
issues.description: The code accesses `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but openForm can be undefined when rendering certain forms (like the main comment form). The original code correctly used `openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet` with optional chaining. This will cause a "Cannot read property 'in_reply_to_snippet' of undefined" runtime error when the FormWrapper is rendered without an openForm prop, crashing the component.

issues.title: Editor editability incorrectly depends on member expertise instead of name
issues.description: The Form component determines whether the editor should be editable by checking `member?.expertise` instead of `memberName` (which is derived from `member?.name`). According to the comment and the original logic, the editor should be disabled only when the member doesn't have a name or when submitting. Expertise is optional metadata, but name is required for posting. This bug prevents users without expertise from typing in the comment editor, even though they have a valid name and should be allowed to comment.

issues.title: Reply threading broken for nested comments due to incorrect in_reply_to_id
issues.description: The submit function uses `parent.id` as `in_reply_to_id` instead of `openForm.in_reply_to_id`. For nested replies (replying to a reply), these values differ: `openForm.in_reply_to_id` points to the specific comment being replied to, while `parent.id` points to the top-level parent comment. Using `parent.id` breaks the reply chain, causing nested replies to be incorrectly threaded to the wrong comment. This destroys the conversation hierarchy and makes it impossible to track which comment a user is actually replying to in multi-level discussions.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25858 - Fixed reply form showing parent comment author's details

structured_output.summary:
The PR aims to stop the reply form header from showing the parent comment author's name and expertise. It removes the `?? comment?.member?.…` fallbacks in `FormWrapper` and `Form`, and drops the `comment` prop from `FormWrapper` and its call site in `reply-form.tsx`. The e2e tests added for the name and expertise cases match that intent. The header fix itself is correct and well covered in spirit.

The PR also makes three changes beyond the stated bug, and they are where the problems are. First, `FormWrapper` now reads `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but `main-form.tsx` renders `FormWrapper` with no `openForm`. Focusing the main comment box will throw during render. Second, `in_reply_to_id` in the reply submit payload is changed from `openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `parent.id`. For reply-to-reply forms, `parent` is the top-level comment, so the reply loses its in_reply_to link, which the server then silently nulls. Third, the editor is now made editable only when the member has `expertise` instead of a `name`. That is an unrequested product change, the nearby comment still says "doesn't have a name", and it leaves the reply form's new e2e test likely to fail on `waitEditorFocused`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: A render-time TypeError on the main comment form (main-form.tsx renders FormWrapper without openForm, and form.tsx:313 dereferences it unguarded) is a crash on a core path and must be fixed. The `in_reply_to_id` change silently breaks reply-to-reply attribution, a regression unrelated to the stated bug. The expertise-gated editor is an unexplained behaviour change that conflicts with its own comment, and the new expertise e2e test is likely to fail as a result. The core name/expertise fallback removal is sound, so the fix is a small, targeted revision.

architecture.overview:
The comments widget renders a single `FormWrapper` (in form.tsx) around a `Form` and `FormHeader` (name, expertise, avatar, replying-to text). Two callers use it: `MainForm` for top-level comments, with no `openForm`, and `ReplyForm` for replies, which receives `openForm` and `parent` from `ReplyFormBox` in comment.tsx. Before this PR, the header and the editor fell back to the comment being replied to when the logged-in member had no name or expertise. That is the source of the bug.

The PR removes those fallbacks, so header values come only from `useAppContext().member`. It also changes two other things: the reply submit payload now sets `in_reply_to_id` from `parent.id` rather than `openForm.in_reply_to_id`, and the editor enablement is keyed on `member.expertise` instead of `member.name`. The server (`comments-service.js`) rejects replies to replies, and it drops `in_reply_to_id` unless the referenced comment shares the same parent.
steps: Entry point: `CommentComponent` in comment.tsx opens a reply form via `openReplyForm`, which dispatches `openCommentForm` with `in_reply_to_id` and `in_reply_to_snippet` set only for reply-to-reply cases.
`ReplyFormBox` (comment.tsx) renders `ReplyForm` with `parent={comment}`. For reply-to-reply, `comment` is the top-level comment because `PublishedComment` owns that form.
`ReplyForm` (reply-form.tsx) wraps `Form` in `FormWrapper` and submits via the `addReply` action. The submit payload is where the `in_reply_to_id` change lands.
`FormWrapper` and `Form` (form.tsx) read the member's name and expertise for `FormHeader` and decide editability. This is where the fallback removal and the expertise gate are.
`MainForm` (main-form.tsx) also renders `FormWrapper`, without `openForm`. Any change in `FormWrapper` that assumes `openForm` exists affects this path.
Server side: `comments-service.js` validates `in_reply_to` against `parent_id`, so an incorrect `in_reply_to_id` is discarded rather than stored, which hides the client-side regression.

findings.title: FormWrapper crashes the main comment form when focused
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx` at line 313, `FormWrapper` reads `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining. `MainForm` in `main-form.tsx` renders `FormWrapper` without an `openForm` prop, so focusing the main comment box throws during render. Restore optional chaining (`openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet`), matching the `openForm?.in_reply_to_id` usage a few lines below. Keep the rest of the PR unchanged.

findings.title: in_reply_to_id now points to the top-level comment in reply-to-reply forms
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx` at line 30, `in_reply_to_id` was changed from `openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `parent.id`. For reply-to-reply forms, `parent` is the top-level comment (see `ReplyFormBox` in `comment.tsx` around line 251), so the reply's real target is lost and the server nulls the field. Restore `in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id` and add `openForm` back to the `useCallback` dependency array. Do not change the header fallback removal in `form.tsx`.

findings.title: Editor editability now keys on expertise, not name, contradicting its comment
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx`, the `useEffect` around lines 258-265 now calls `editor.setEditable(!!member?.expertise && progress !== 'sending')`, but its comment says editing is disabled when the member has no name, and `focusEditor` (around line 356) still gates on `memberName`. Decide on one rule. The header fix does not require changing editability. Most likely, restore the `memberName` gate and keep the dependency on `memberName`, or, if expertise gating is intended, update the comment and `focusEditor` together and call it out in the PR description.

findings.title: Expertise e2e test likely fails because the editor is non-editable
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts` around lines 614-649, the test `Reply form does not inherit expertise from parent comment author` calls `waitEditorFocused(editor)` at line 639 for a member with `expertise: null`. The PR's `setEditable(!!member?.expertise)` gate makes that editor non-editable, so focus will never arrive. Either revert the editability gate (see the related finding in form.tsx), or remove the focus wait and assert the header contents only. Keep the existing assertions for `member-name` and the `Add your expertise` text.

findings.title: Name-absence e2e assertion passes vacuously and asserts nothing about the placeholder
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts` around lines 676-679, the assertion `expect(memberName).not.toHaveText('Named Author')` is weak because it can pass without checking the header. `FormHeader` in `form.tsx` renders `name ? name : 'Anonymous'` inside the `member-name` test id. Replace the negative assertion with a positive `toHaveText('Anonymous')` (keeping the comment explaining why the parent's name must not appear). This follows the style of the other assertions in the file.

findings.title: Unrelated class reordering in reply-form.tsx
findings.body:
`mt-[-16px] pr-2` was reordered to `pr-2 mt-[-16px]`. That is cosmetic churn in a PR about a logic bug, and it adds noise to the review. Revert it so the diff contains only the functional change.

findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx` at line 47, the class string was changed from `mt-[-16px] pr-2` to `pr-2 mt-[-16px]` with no functional effect. Restore the original order so the PR diff only contains the intended logic change.

findings.title: Removing the name and expertise fallbacks fixes the reported header bug
findings.body:
The core change is right. `FormWrapper` and `Form` now read `member?.name` and `member?.expertise` directly, with no `comment?.member` fallback. A logged-in member with no name or expertise now gets the placeholder, not the parent author's details. The removed `comment` prop from `FormWrapper` also eliminates the path that caused the bug.
